summaries.summary: The page explains evaporation and its relationship to heat and water, focusing on latent heat of evaporation and hydrogen bonding. It describes how only the fastest-moving molecules evaporate, leaving lower-energy molecules behind. A diagram shows evaporation and includes a note that evaporation which has reached equilibrium with the liquid surface is said to have reached saturation.
key_facts: Latent heat of evaporation is the heat energy needed to evaporate a substance.
Water has a high latent heat of evaporation due to hydrogen bonding.
Only fastest-moving molecules evaporate; lower-energy molecules remain.
Evaporation which has reached equilibrium with the liquid surface is said to have reached saturation.
